evidence_items.publisher: Kevin Zheyuan Cui and coauthors; September 2024 working paper, mirrored by Readwise
evidence_items.explanation: The September analysis pooled three field experiments involving 4,867 developers and estimated increased completed-task output far below tenfold. The 26.08% figure is the pooled estimate, not an estimate exclusively for junior developers.

Uplevel found no meaningful efficiency improvement in its measured development metrics across 785 developers, comparing early 2023 with early 2024. This supports the productivity assessment; its findings about bugs are not used to score the possibility caveat.

This controlled HTTP-server programming experiment found a substantial task-time benefit, qualifying any suggestion that all benefits were small. It nevertheless falls well short of tenfold productivity and supports the explicitly comparative reading.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not supply a common measure of total, long-term programmer productivity.
Uplevel's exact initial publication date is not stated in the retrieved report; September 17 is the verified contemporaneous coverage date.
